questions.question: Find the average of the 6 terms 3, 6, 12, 24, 48 and 96.
A training centre has 80 candidates. Successful candidates average 76 marks, unsuccessful candidates average 44 marks, and all candidates average 68. How many candidates were successful?
questions.explanation: Successful fraction = (68 − 44) ÷ (76 − 44) = 3/4. Successful count = 80 × 3/4 = 60.

questions.question: A group averages 45 kg. 3 members averaging 41 kg leave and 5 averaging 57 kg join. The new average is 48 kg. Find the original number of members.
questions.explanation: For original count n, 45n − 3 × 41 + 5 × 57 = 48(n + 2). Thus 3n = 66 and n = 22.

questions.question: 9 numbers average 32. The first 4 total 116 and the last 4 total 134. Find the middle number.
questions.explanation: Middle number = 9 × 32 − 116 − 134 = 38.

questions.question: The average of the first n positive odd integers is 37. Find n.
questions.explanation: The average of the first n positive odd integers is n. Hence n = 37.

questions.question: A class has 24 pupils averaging 13 years. Their teacher is included, and after 2 years the same 25 people average 16 years. Find the teacher’s present age in years.
questions.explanation: Today’s combined average = 16 − 2 = 14. Teacher’s present age = 25 × 14 − 24 × 13 = 38 years.

questions.question: Equal amounts of money are spent on tea priced at ₹240 and ₹360 per kg. Find the average purchase price per kg in ₹.
questions.explanation: For equal expenditure, average price = 2 × 240 × 360 ÷ (240 + 360) = ₹288 per kg.

questions.question: 3 groups contain 10, 15 and 25 workers with average outputs of 24, 28 and 32 units. Find the average output per worker.
11 readings average 40. The first 5 average 36 and the last 5 average 43. If the 6th reading is increased by 21, what will be the average of the first 6 readings?
The average of 5 numbers is 62. 4 have deviations 8, −5, 3 and −10 from 62. Find the 5th number.
questions.explanation: Deviations must sum to 0, so the 5th deviation is 4. 5th number = 62 + 4 = 66.

questions.question: A team of 25 averages 64 points. 5 players leave, and the remaining average rises to 67. Find the average points of those who left.
questions.explanation: Departing average = 64 − 20 × (67 − 64) ÷ 5 = 52.

questions.question: A cyclist covers equal distances at 18 and 30 km/h. How many minutes are needed to cover 90 km at the resulting average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = 2 × 18 × 30 ÷ 48 = 22.5 km/h. Time = 90 ÷ 22.5 × 60 = 240 minutes.

questions.question: 30 measurements average 48. entries were recorded as 83 and 26 instead of 38 and 62. Find the corrected average.
questions.explanation: Total correction = 38 + 62 − 83 − 26 = −9. Correct average = 48 − 9 ÷ 30 = 47.7.

questions.question: Find the average of all 2-digit positive integers divisible by 13.
questions.explanation: The sequence runs from 13 to 91. Average = (13 + 91) ÷ 2 = 52.

questions.question: A club has 14 members averaging 40 years. How many members averaging 28 years must join to reduce the average to 36 years?
questions.explanation: Existing excess = 14 × (40 − 36) = 56 years. Each newcomer offsets 36 − 28 = 8 years, so 56 ÷ 8 = 7 join.

questions.question: 40 players average 60 kg. 4 players averaging 52 kg are replaced, raising the group average to 61.2 kg. The new players’ weights are in ratio 1 : 2 : 2 : 3. Find the heaviest new player’s weight in kg.
questions.explanation: New players total = 4 × 52 + 40 × 1.2 = 256 kg. Heaviest = 256 × 3 ÷ 8 = 96 kg.

questions.question: A batter averages 38 runs per innings in 15 innings. In his next 2 innings he scores 54 and 73. Find his new average runs per innings.
questions.explanation: Extra above the old base = 54 + 73 − 2 × 38 = 51. New average = 38 + 51 ÷ 17 = 41.

questions.question: Permanent workers average ₹900 per day and temporary workers ₹600. The combined average is ₹780. What percentage of workers are permanent?
questions.explanation: Permanent fraction = (780 − 600) ÷ (900 − 600) = 3/5. Percentage = 60%.

questions.question: A bowler concedes 52 runs in 6 overs and 3 legal balls. Find his average runs conceded per over, taking 6 legal balls per over.
questions.explanation: 6 overs and 3 balls = 6.5 overs, not 6.3. Runs per over = 52 ÷ 6.5 = 8.

questions.question: 11 friends share a meal. 7 pay ₹180 each, 3 pay ₹240 each, and the organiser pays ₹120 more than the average payment of all 11. Find the organiser’s payment in ₹.
questions.explanation: If the average is x, then 7 × 180 + 3 × 240 + x + 120 = 11x, giving x = 210. Organiser pays 210 + 120 = ₹330.

questions.question: A candidate averages 64 marks in 3 equally weighted papers. The fourth paper carries double the weight of each earlier paper. What mark in it gives a final weighted average of 70?
questions.explanation: Total weight = 3 + 2 = 5. Required mark = (5 × 70 − 3 × 64) ÷ 2 = 79.

questions.question: A worker earns ₹700 per day for 6 days. Find his average daily income over the full 7-day week if he earns 0 on the 7th day.
questions.explanation: Weekly income = 6 × 700 = ₹4200. Daily average = 4200 ÷ 7 = ₹600.

questions.question: A delivery van covers 150 km in 3 hours and 90 km in 2 hours. Its overall average including 1 halt is 40 km/h. Find the halt duration in minutes.
questions.explanation: Total time = 240 ÷ 40 = 6 hours; moving time = 3 + 2 = 5 hours. Halt = (6 − 5) × 60 = 60 minutes.

questions.question: Is the average of 4 real numbers greater than 25? I: Each of the 3 smallest numbers exceeds 20, and the largest exceeds 40. II: All 4 numbers are positive. Choose the code: 1 = I alone is sufficient; 2 = II alone is sufficient; 3 = both together are needed and sufficient; 4 = both together are insufficient.
questions.explanation: I forces the total above 3 × 20 + 40 = 100, hence the mean exceeds 25. II only forces the mean above 0, so I alone is sufficient.

questions.question: A father and daughter average 34 years, and their ages are in ratio 13 : 4. Find the daughter’s age after 5 years, in years.
questions.explanation: Daughter’s present age = 2 × 34 × 4 ÷ 17 = 16. After 5 years, she will be 21.
